submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is a retrospective content-word dial on the current token: activation runs from about -0.3 on the closed-class words that only structure a clause ('the', 'are', 'have', 'can', 'they', 'their', 'In', 'If', 'it', 'one'), through ordinary nouns, verbs and adjectives, up to +0.2 and beyond on rare, technical and proper-name tokens, so within a short declarative the peak lands on the predicate or complement that carries the clause's content ('landed' 0.64, 'brown' 0.63, 'Paris' 0.59, 'noon' 0.51, 'raised' 0.47, 'cities' 0.41, 'converts' 0.40) rather than on the subject-and-function-word frame (within-document mean content minus function = +0.10, content above function in 110 of 112 documents; the highest-frequency grammatical tokens are the strongest negatives: 'The' -0.40, 'If' -0.31, 'In' -0.30, 'were' -0.30, 'could' -0.29, 'they' -0.28, 'their' -0.28, 'its' -0.27, 'I' -0.27, 'have' -0.26, 'can' -0.26). It is local (58% of a peak's input attribution sits on the peak token itself, 15% on the token before) and not lookahead (zero-ablating the positive pole moves next-token probabilities by KL = 4e-4 and its Jacobian-lens promotions ' sequentially', ' utilizing', ' defining' never follow a peak); the acknowledged residue is the function word that opens a content-bearing complement, where the peak can sit on the preposition or determiner of the phrase (' at' 0.67, ' the' 0.54/0.59, ' à' 0.71) instead of on the content word inside it, which the lexical axis alone does not explain.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is what it is, and that is all that it can be.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A vacuous copular chain built only from closed-class tokens ('it', 'is', 'what', 'that', 'all', 'can', 'be'), so the content-word dial predicts the negative band and no token should reach the positive pole.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: If they were, they would have been, and if they had, it would be as it was.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A conditional chain made entirely of the hypothesis's own strongest negatives ('If', 'they', 'were', 'would', 'have', 'been', 'it', 'as', 'was'), so it should sit near the closed-class floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Only when it is as it is for them can it be for us, and not until then.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A temporal/prepositional frame of pure function words ('only', 'when', 'it', 'is', 'as', 'for', 'them', 'can', 'be', 'us', 'not', 'then') tests whether the acknowledged ' at the' residue requires a real content complement rather than firing on bare function words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Could it have been them, or was it us, and who is it for?
adversarial_test_results.detail: An interrogative of auxiliaries, pronouns and wh-words about agency, all closed-class, so the lexical dial predicts the negative band even though the sentence is syntactically about who did what to whom.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Ce n'est que ce qu'il est, et ce n'est pas ce que ce fut.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French text in the same register as top example 1 but stripped of every content word, testing whether the French function-word frame alone produces the ' à'-type peak or whether a content complement is required.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Wenn es so wäre, hätte es nicht sein können, und doch ist es, wie es war.
adversarial_test_results.detail: German conditional with no content words; since the hypothesis's axis is lexical (closed-class versus content), its closed-class floor should hold in a language not represented among the examples.

The same markup frame as top example 6 with every content word removed, so the dial predicts no natural-language content word and any peak here would be a delimiter or massive-activation artifact rather than the claimed lexical effect.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yes. No. Not yet. Well, then. So be it. As if.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A run of interjections and deictic function words spread across sentence-initial and list positions tests the claim that the dial is lexical rather than positional, since no token here carries clause content.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This? That? Those? Which one, then? Not these. Not any. Each of them, or none at all. Here and there, and there and here?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Demonstratives, quantifiers and pronouns only, including 'one' and 'these', which the hypothesis places at the negative end; the multi-line question and list structure also varies position and delimiters.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In that it is for them, it is not for us; and if it were not so, it would be as it has been. What they would have it be, it can be, and what it is, it is. For them, and by them, and to them, it is only what it is.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A longer (~55-token) content-free passage with a conditional and a purpose clause tests the negative band at depth, not only in short snippets, as the hypothesis's closed-class floor should be stable across length.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I have a can and a will, but they were not mine.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same tokens in other senses: the modals 'can' and 'will' appear as content nouns ('a can', 'a will'), but the hypothesis scores the token and lists 'can' and 'have' among its strongest negatives, so it predicts the closed-class floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lessee shall indemnify the licensor against all claims arising from the licensed patent.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A legal-contract sentence from a genre absent from the scan examples, dense with rare technical nouns and a content-carrying predicate ('indemnify', 'licensor', 'patent'), which the rare-technical end of the dial predicts should peak well above zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her cello solo in the second movement drifts above a muted pizzicato accompaniment.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A music-review holdout using rare instrument and performance terms ('cello', 'pizzicato', 'accompaniment') with none of the claimed trigger tokens, so the dial predicts a positive peak on one of these content words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The antibody binds the CD4 receptor with nanomolar affinity.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An immunology holdout whose short declarative shape matches the top examples but whose rare technical token ('CD4', 'nanomolar') and content predicate ('binds') are new, so the hypothesis predicts activation on the predicate or complement.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At Vicarage Road on Tuesday, Okafor's header sealed the win for Watford.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A sports report packed with proper names ('Vicarage Road', 'Okafor', 'Watford') from a new genre, testing the proper-name end of the dial and the claim that a preposition can open a content-bearing complement.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Morning on the reserve began with fog lying low over the reed beds, and for a long while nothing moved except the water and the slow drift of mist between the willows. The warden walked the eastern path with a notebook in his coat pocket, counting what he could and writing down what he could not name. By eight the sun had burned through, and the air filled with the sound of warblers working through the scrub while a pair of marsh harriers quartered the far field. He stopped at the third hide, where the boards had rotted through in the winter, and made a note about the repairs that would be needed before the season opened to visitors. Two hours later he reached the far boundary, where the old drainage channel runs straight as a ruled line toward the sea, and where the bank had slumped into the water after the spring floods. It was there, in the dark mud at the edge of the channel, that he found the shell of a freshwater mussel, and beside it a fragment of a Roman amphora, its rim still sharp and its curve still true after two thousand years in the silt. He photographed both, marked the position on his map, and walked back along the seawall to the office, where the kettle was still warm and the logbook lay open at the wrong page. That evening, over tea, he read the entry aloud to the volunteer who had come to help with the survey, and the two of them argued amiably about whether the amphora had been carried up the channel by a trader or dropped there by a farmer who had found it in a field and thought it worthless. Neither could settle it, so they wrote down both possibilities, dated the page, and left the question for someone with more patience and a better library.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long nature-writing passage (~330 words) with rare content words such as 'amphora' and 'mussel' buried deep inside tests the local, retrospective claim that the dial still peaks on rare content tokens far into a passage rather than only in short snippets.
